prompt: Why does the clock’s first tick seem to last longer?

options.text: The brain extends the hand’s image backwards, to before the eyes moved
The clock really slows down when watched
The eyes get tired from focusing

explanation: The brain fills in the eye jump by stretching the target’s image back in time.
misconception: The clock doesn’t change: time perception adjusts after the eye movement.

prompt: How often does the brain do this stretching?

options.text: Every time we move our eyes, but we only notice with a time reference
Only when we look at clocks

explanation: It happens with every eye movement; the second hand just makes the effect visible.
